newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pajaritos port reopened - Transport Min.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pajaritos port reopened - Transport Min.

text.p: Mexico's key crude port Pajaritos on the Gulf of Mexico reopened on Saturday after being closed because of high winds, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said.

Seven ports on the gulf coast had shipping either halted completed or restricted to the only the sturdiest craft earlier on Saturday because of 40 mph (60 kph) winds, and only the port of Veracruz remained closed on Saturday afternoon, the SCT said in a report.
The forceful winds remained at Veracruz with waves of up to six feet (two meters) and cloudy skies, the SCT said.
A warning remained in place for small boats in the northern Gulf of Mexico, the state of Tamaulipas and northern Veracruz state because of strong winds and choppy seas, the ministry said.

The goverment news agency Notimex reported earlier Saturday that 13 ships had been prevented from sailing out of Veracruz Bay, two others were beached on the island of Sacrificios and 20 fishing boats had taken refuge at a nearby Navy base.
Mexico's National Meteorological Service said a cold front coming from the north was causing inclement weather in much of northeastern and eastern Mexico.
